title: Acute kidney injury onset prediction
summary: Candidate design coordinates for predicting incident AKI from longitudinal ICU data. Confirm baseline kidney status, measurement cadence, prediction horizon, and whether both creatinine and urine-output definitions are observable before adopting the card.

design_candidates.population: Adult ICU stays at risk for a new AKI event; pre-existing renal dysfunction and renal-replacement therapy require explicit, question-specific handling rather than automatic exclusion.
design_candidates.time_zero: A clinically observable landmark such as ICU admission or a rolling prediction landmark, fixed before the prediction window.
design_candidates.observation_window: Use only measurements available before each landmark; document baseline creatinine ascertainment and urine-output completeness.
design_candidates.prediction_or_followup_window: Choose and justify a clinically useful near-term horizon; prevent overlap between feature and outcome windows.
eligibility_candidates: Confirm patients are event-free at the landmark
Report availability of baseline creatinine and urine output separately
design_candidates.exposure: A prespecified predictor set measured before the landmark, not a post-outcome proxy.
design_candidates.outcome: Incident AKI stage derived from an explicitly implementable KDIGO-aligned creatinine and/or urine-output rule.
design_candidates.estimand: Risk of a new AKI event within the declared horizon among patients event-free and observable at the landmark.
recommended_methods: Patient-level temporal split or external validation
Preprocessing fitted within each training fold

stop_conditions: AKI onset cannot be temporally separated from predictors
Neither creatinine nor urine output supports an implementable outcome
requires_confirmation: Confirm whether pre-existing kidney disease or renal-replacement therapy changes eligibility
Confirm the AKI definition components and prediction horizon before planning
